entries.title: 5 ways to upgrade your study habits with Chrome
entries.summary: The video shows a whiteboard that says "Keeping Tabs on Google Chrome."
entries.content:
Whether you’re trying to wrap your head around a tough chemistry concept or keep your research organized, here are five ways Chrome can help you get the most out of the school year.

1. Dive deeper into new subjects.

Gemini in Chrome is already a powerful tool for learning about complex topics, letting you ask questions about the research paper you’re citing, visualize a concept you’re struggling to understand, or find the relevant part of a YouTube lecture. To help you get more out of all of the educational content the web has to offer, we’re expanding these capabilities on desktop to include even more types of media, like podcasts and videos on sites other than YouTube.

Listening to a podcast on ancient Rome, or reviewing a recording of your last philosophy lecture? Gemini in Chrome can identify key takeaways, find specific information, or clarify confusing moments for almost any audio or video file once you’ve played it through.

2. Test your knowledge to make concepts stick.

Reading your notes helps, but testing your knowledge is what makes a lesson stick. To help you get the most out of your study guide, Gemini in Chrome can now generate interactive quizzes using the content from your tab. Whether it’s a Google Doc of your physics notes, a research paper on the Byzantine Empire, or a YouTube video about machine learning, Chrome can highlight core concepts and help you check your understanding. This feature is rolling out in English in the U.S. and India on desktop and will be expanding to additional regions and mobile in the coming months.

3. Stay organized for class.

Managing papers and projects across multiple classes often means opening dozens of tabs, creating digital clutter that can derail your focus. Whether you prefer to display your tabs vertically or horizontally, with tab groups you can bring order to the chaos by organizing them based on your courses or projects.

But even with your tabs nicely organized, jumping back and forth between pages can break your concentration. That’s where split view comes in, letting you keep reference materials on one side of your screen while you’re drafting a paper on the other. Because paired tabs stay linked together, you can step away or switch tasks and jump right back into your side-by-side workspace when you’re ready.

4. Learn on any device.

When you're deep into a research session, you don’t want to lose your progress when you step away from your computer. You can already send a tab from your laptop to your phone (or vice versa), but now Chrome makes switching between devices even easier by saving the exact state of your tab when you send it over. This includes your scroll position and partially filled forms. So if you're halfway through a 50-page paper on behavioral economics, you can send it to your phone and pick up exactly where you left during your commute.

5. Customize your study routine.

Chrome is designed to adapt to your unique learning preferences. If you get distracted by cluttered websites, immersive reading mode strips away the visual noise so you can focus on the text. You can even change the font, letter spacing, and contrast level if you struggle to read dense blocks of text.

And if you want to listen to your study materials while you’re on the go or resting your eyes after a long day, Chrome’s read aloud tool will narrate the page. On Android, read aloud’s AI playback capability can even generate a podcast-like conversation based on the page you're viewing.

The school year might be well underway, but it’s never too late to upgrade your study habits. From keeping your tabs tidy to helping you understand tough topics with Gemini, Chrome is the ultimate study buddy for whatever challenges the academic year throws at you.

entries.title: 5 Google Photos updates to make the most of summer memories.
entries.summary: Five updates in Google Photos that will help you make the most of your summer memories.
entries.content:
Summer trips are wrapped, and your photo library is packed. Here are five Google Photos updates that will help you make the most of your memories.

  • Select, brighten and share the best family portraits from a weekend getaway with a single prompt using Photos in Gemini Spark. 1
  • Curate your ultimate digital closet with wardrobe, which automatically catalogs the clothing in your photos and lets you virtually style and try on new looks. 2
  • Give your photos a nostalgic, vintage-inspired look with Moods. Edit with styles that intelligently adapt to your images, like 35mm film, 2000s digicam, and more. 3
  • Turn everyday memories into red carpet moments, whimsical birthday cards, photo booth shots, and more with 15 new Remix templates. 4
  • Try the upgraded markup tool, which gives you a redact pen to blur sensitive info, precise thickness sliders for custom sketches, and fresh fonts to make your text pop. 5

entries.title: Our new health and safety tools are live in the Google Health app.
entries.summary: Pixel Watch users can explore the new health and safety tools in the Google Health app.
entries.content:
Health Guardian features 1 , our new proactive health and safety tools, are rolling out in the Google Health app, giving Pixel Watch users more ways to prioritize their well-being directly from their wrists. Users can set up blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and sleep breathing quality metrics in the app beginning this week. The tools will be included free with Pixel Watch 3, 4, and 5 devices, with the first trend reports arriving in early October. 2

Fitbit Air users will be able to see their insulin resistance and blood pressure trends with a Google Health Premium subscription later this year.

Backed by clinical research, the new Health Guardian features work continuously in the background to track subtle physiological shifts over time. The Health Guardian features suite also includes our first-of-its-kind Breathing Emergency Detection for Pixel Watch 4 and 5 users in select European countries. It’s designed to automatically prompt a call to emergency services if a user experiences severe drops in blood oxygen. 3

entries.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar
entries.summary: an image with the phrase "Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar"
entries.content:
Building on the momentum of last week's Gemini 3.8 Live launch, today we are excited to introduce Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar — bringing near real-time visual presence to our native live dialogue models. By pairing near real-time video generation with speech, the Live Avatar feature creates an experience that listens, sees, and speaks with a dynamic visual persona.

With precise lip-syncing, natural expressions, and fluid turn-taking, Live Avatar enables enterprises to expand their virtual offerings more interactively. Whether providing engaging customer service or delivering interactive walkthroughs, it transforms digital exchanges into richer, more accessible experiences.

Starting today, Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar is available in Gemini Enterprise.

See how Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar supports a wide range of characters, each with a distinct look, voice, and expressive presence.

More natural and multimodal conversations

Conversation is inherently multimodal: we listen, look, speak, and use facial expressions to communicate. Live Avatar brings these capabilities to enterprise agents. By processing visual and audio inputs simultaneously, it generates enriching conversations for a more comprehensive experience.

Watch how Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar takes in what it sees and hears in near real time, responding with expressive audio and video for a more natural conversation.

Asynchronous tool execution with continuous presence

Beyond visual presence, the feature is backed by Gemini’s advanced reasoning. With asynchronous tool calling, Live Avatar can trigger tool calls and fetch data in the background while continuing active dialogue, handling complex tasks while ensuring an uninterrupted conversational flow.

See how Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar handles complex tasks like checking in a guest at a hotel. Calling tools in the background while the dialogue continues uninterrupted.

Conversational experiences built for global scale

Conversational presence should feel natural and not be limited by languages. Live Avatar features native multilingual speech-to-speech synchronization. The feature dynamically adapts its lip-sync and expressions and can seamlessly transition across 97 languages without degrading video fidelity or introducing visual drift.

Watch how Gemini 3.8 Live Avatar switches between languages mid-conversation, with lip-sync and expressions adapting seamlessly across 97 languages.

A Live Avatar to fit your brand needs

Organizations often need distinct visual identities to fit their brand. In addition to a library of diverse, preset avatars, organizations can customize their Live Avatars. From a high-quality reference image, developers can generate a fully animated, responsive avatar while preserving reference likeness, brand styling, or character identity. Custom avatar creation is currently available only through enterprise allowlisting.

Trust and transparency at its core

We built Live Avatar with strict safeguards designed to respect identity, and keep AI-generated content transparent. All output generated by our AI products is watermarked with SynthID. This imperceptible watermark is woven directly into the audio and video output, helping to ensure AI-generated content remains detectable to help minimise misinformation and misattribution. To explore our comprehensive approach to safety and responsible deployment, read our model card.

Get started with Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar

Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar is available in Gemini Enterprise. Explore the API documentation to get started.

entries.title: Behind Project Suncatcher, our moonshot to put AI in space
entries.summary: A yellow, red, and blue gradient background with the words Project Suncatcher overlaid
entries.content:
After years of research, Project Suncatcher is scheduled to embark on its first test in orbit, launching a prototype satellite to evaluate how Google Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) perform in space.

Announced last year, Project Suncatcher is a long-term, research moonshot exploring whether space could one day host scalable machine learning infrastructure. In low Earth orbit, satellites can access near-constant sunlight, generating up to eight times more solar power than on Earth. Eventually, it could be possible to link together multiple constellations of satellites, allowing them to manage larger AI workloads while in orbit.

Big breakthroughs happen when you work backwards from an end goal. In our case, it's to ensure AI's profound benefits in key areas, from healthcare to scientific discovery, can reach everyone, far into the future. Just as early research into autonomous driving and quantum computing required years of experimentation before we got to practical systems, exploring compute in space begins with measured, deliberate steps.

Turning that idea into reality starts with a basic question: Can our AI hardware operate in space? This initial mission onboard the upcoming Transporter-18 rideshare mission with SpaceX was developed in partnership with Planet. It’s designed to gather in-orbit data on how our TPUs handle the physical stress of spaceflight and the radiation and thermal extremes of space.

As we prepare for an early test launch and work toward our next milestone in 2027, the Project Suncatcher team discussed what we hope to learn and the engineering hurdles ahead in a new video series digging into the science behind the mission.

Hardware survival

A rocket trip into low Earth orbit lasts about 10 minutes, during which the spacecraft experiences intense vibration and sustained acceleration loads up to 10 times the force of gravity, or g-force. Individual components, such as the TPU chips, can experience even greater forces up to 50 to 100 g. The team conducted vibration testing by intensely shaking the satellite on all three axes to mimic the frequencies of a rocket launch. Tests like this rarely go as planned, so we were pleasantly surprised that the hardware held up to the force.

Once the TPU chips make it to space, the level of radiation outside the Earth’s atmosphere presents another challenge to overcome. Solar events and cosmic rays can wreak havoc on electronics, so our team tested TPUs in a proton beam facility at UC Davis’s Crocker Nuclear Laboratory while running AI workloads. During the test, we monitored closely to see how errors, like a bitflip, would affect our workloads. Initial results have shown that our Trillium TPUs hold up remarkably well, and can survive a radiation total ionizing dose greater than what they would receive during a five-year space mission.

But some things can only be tested in space. Putting our first TPUs in orbit next week will help us get data and learnings to inform future launches.

Cooling in space

Cooling orbital data centers is a crucial research challenge. TPUs generate a large amount of heat in a small area, which needs to be diffused safely or the chips are at risk of overheating. But in space, there’s no airflow. In a vacuum, you can only diffuse heat via radiators, which requires a totally different approach to cooling electronics.

We’re working on a number of different approaches for this, including a combination of heat pipes and radiators to cool the chips. So far, our team has tested the technology in a thermal vacuum chamber that simulates both the thermal and vacuum environment in space. We’ll see how our new TPU cooling system works in space and refine our designs as we learn more.

Satellite interconnectivity

Future designs of our satellites will each carry dozens of TPU chips while orbiting the Earth in clusters. To maintain the bandwidth necessary to process AI, every satellite has to know both its own position and where it sits relative to its neighbors. To do this, the satellites will communicate via lasers.

The technology in space already exists, but most state-of-the-art systems are optimized for low bandwidth across large distances, whereas our lasers need to operate at very high bandwidth over extremely short distances. Maintaining the necessary connection requires extraordinary precision, similar to hitting a coin-size target from miles away while both points are in motion. We’ll test our work on this in 2027 when we put two satellites in orbit.

Just the beginning

Exploring space as a viable location for scalable AI compute won’t happen all at once. It takes methodical engineering, starting with proving our hardware can handle the physical and unpredictable realities of operating in orbit. This first launch is about seeing what works, identifying points of failure, and applying those findings to future missions.

Every transformative technology we’ve built at Google began with an audacious goal — and the discipline of working backward to solve hard problems all along the way. As our latest moonshot heads to the launchpad, our team is excited to share what we learn and the science driving this work forward.

entries.title: Helping 25,000 veterans and military families build careers in skilled trades
entries.summary: A man with a beard, wearing clear safety glasses, gray work gloves, and a dark short-sleeved polo shirt, works on electrical wiring or panels in an industrial setting.
entries.content:
Most of my career has been in the U.S. Navy. I served for seven years as a nuclear-trained operator and 13 years as a submarine officer. Transitioning to a civilian role was a tall order — and if not for the help and support of my network, I’m not sure I would have found a role that made the most of my expertise while offering a feeling of accomplishment. Luckily for me, my former shipmate helped me land an interview for a role managing data center engineering operations.

It turns out, a lot of the skills you pick up running a nuclear submarine (planning and leading a mission, working closely with technicians, exercising sound judgment) are the same kinds of skills that come in handy when your job is to oversee data center operations. And now Google is making it easier for veterans to make career transitions to high-growth careers like mine.

Today, Google is launching a commitment to help 25,000 veterans and military family members build rewarding careers in skilled trades. Funding and support from Google.org will go to the organizations who know this community best: Hiring Our Heroes, Student Veterans of America (SVA), and Home Builders Institute (HBI). Together, they’re offering hands-on pre-apprenticeships, career coaching, and even direct job placements.

As a leader for Google’s data centers in Ohio and Indiana, I know there’s a major need for these types of professionals. Currently there are hundreds of thousands of skilled trade roles open across the U.S. just waiting to be filled. These are jobs like master electrician, lead pipefitter, and project manager — high-growth careers that offer long-term financial stability.

But beyond just the growing need, these roles also make the most of the kinds of skills veterans and military families know better than anyone — skills like problem-solving under pressure, teamwork, and getting a job done right.

Google has a long history of supporting veterans and the skilled trades. Earlier this year, Google joined forces with BlackRock, Ford, and Carhartt to launch the Alliance for America's Skilled Trades. With funding from Google.org, Google also supported the electrical training Alliance (etA) to put AI-powered learning tools on the trade floor, and provided funding to SVA to bring Google Career Certificates and AI courses to veterans nationwide. This is all part of Google.org’s broader AI Opportunity Fund for the United States, ensuring Americans benefit from this evolving technology.

With today’s announcement, they’re going even further and making it easier than ever for veterans and military families to access opportunities that will lead to rewarding careers.

I will always be grateful for the path I found after my service, and today I’m glad to see that even more veterans and their families will be able to access career opportunities that continue to offer a chance to serve their communities and country.

entries.title: Turning cultural artifacts into interactive learning companions
entries.summary: A split image showing "Museum Memory" in white text over faint classical statues on a pink background, next to "The Talking Museum" alongside an astronaut with a soundwave speech bubble on a light beige background.
entries.content:
What if museum artifacts could talk? Google Arts & Culture Lab explores this concept with The Talking Museum, a Gemini-assisted experience that lets you get an up-close look at almost 200 3D cultural objects — and ask them questions. Google Arts & Culture Lab is also debuting Museum Memory, an interactive game that challenges players to restore scrambled art gallery exhibitions.

Both experiments are part of Google Arts & Culture Lab’s artist residency program and ongoing efforts to utilize technology to connect people to culture in new ways.

The Talking Museum brings artifacts to life.

Google Arts & Culture Lab artist in residence Lex Fefegha created The Talking Museum to bring an array of cultural objects — spanning prehistoric times to the present day — into a virtual study room.

The Talking Museum invites you to explore more than 190 cultural artifacts from Google Arts & Culture partners. Browse artifacts by size, material, or era, and bring individual artifacts into your virtual study room. Uncover the history of each artifact by listening to Gemini-powered audio commentary, and ask questions as you zoom in on or rotate each piece for a full 360-degree view. Hotspots help you discover unique points of interest as Gemini guides you through the stories behind the artifacts.

Museum Memory tests your recall.

Game designer Carol Mertz and game developer Mary McKenzie created Museum Memory, which is set inside a virtual museum gallery and requires a good memory and a sharp eye.

To play the game, you first observe how paintings are hung in a virtual exhibition space and do your best to memorize the placement of each artwork. Once time is up, the paintings are scrambled, and it's up to you to restore the exhibition. It’s a fun, easy way to train your memory — and discover works of art along the way.

Test your observation skills by restoring scrambled exhibitions in this interactive game.

Head to Google Arts & Culture to explore these experiments and many more.

entries.title: Anyone can make stunning HD videos with Gemini Omni in Google Vids
entries.summary: Google Vids logo surrounded by various video editing options
entries.content:
We’re bringing the magic of video creation to everyone by expanding access to Google Vids. Now anyone with a Google or Google Workspace account can generate high-quality videos at no cost using our latest Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash model and new creative controls. Whether you’re launching a business, rallying a community, or showcasing a product, you can use Google’s most advanced AI to create inspiring videos without professional editing skills or a big budget.

Watch how anyone can generate and edit high-definition video scenes using Omni 1.1 in Google Vids at no cost.

Try it by visiting vids.new on desktop and selecting "Create AI videos."

Select “Create AI videos” from the Google Vids creation menu to start generating scenes with Omni 1.1 at no cost.

Direct your story, don't just prompt it.

Omni 1.1 in Google Vids gives you control of your videos from the first concept to the final export, so you can direct every detail to match your creative vision.

  • Extend scenes with smooth transitions: Make scenes last longer while keeping the visual context, lighting, characters’ appearance, and the environment consistent.
  • Set super-specific durations: Choose the exact duration of your generated clip so it aligns precisely with your story and voiceover.
  • Generate in HD: Create brand-new AI video scenes in full 1080p HD, or upscale existing AI clips to blend seamlessly across your timeline.

Build for any audience.

Whether you’re working on a side project or managing a global campaign, these new controls adapt to your creative goals.

  • For the side hustler launching a new product: Pick a ready-to-use video template to launch your next product without manual video editing.
  • For the local business owner: Snap a few pictures of new arrivals and quickly turn them into promo videos to show your community what's in stock.
  • For enterprise marketing teams: Produce eye-catching videos for landing pages, social announcements, and digital event signage.
  • For community organizers: Create a video to spread the word about local events, clubs, or community fundraisers.

Create and share with transparency.

Creativity has to go hand in hand with transparency. Every clip generated with Omni 1.1 in Google Vids includes an imperceptible SynthID digital watermark embedded into the video frames. This allows viewers to verify that content was generated with AI.

Narrate with just a few keystrokes.

Coming soon, Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite text-to-speech in Google Vids will turn any script into a natural-sounding voiceover across 100+ languages. Whether you’re a creator making social media clips or a business owner explaining a new service, you can generate clear narration simply by typing.

Start building today.

Ready to turn your vision into reality? Anyone with a Google or Google Workspace account can sign into Google Vids and start generating videos with Omni 1.1 at no cost.

For more access to AI video generation in Google Vids on your personal account, explore our Google AI plans. For teams needing greater capacity and management, Workspace Business and Enterprise plans include expanded generation pools and centralized admin controls. Explore details on the Google Workspace Learning Center.

Bring your next idea to life at vids.new.

entries.title: Google Beam expands with new regions, partners, and customers
entries.content:
Since its early days, Google Beam has been driven by a singular vision: bringing people together so they can experience genuine, face-to-face connection, no matter the distance. We’ve tested Beam with early users, including in our own offices, and shown how it can help transform everyday meetings into authentic moments of connection.

Today, we’re announcing a major expansion of our global footprint, new data on our proven impact, and the launch of our first-ever extended network.

Expanding our global footprint

We are officially expanding our global reach, with Google Beam units shipping to customers across six countries, including the U.S., Canada, U.K., France, Germany, and Japan. Backing this rollout is a robust, global ecosystem of 18 channel partners who are fully equipped to deploy and support Beam.

Delivered by our flagship hardware partner as HP Dimension with Google Beam, this experience is built for modern enterprise collaboration. By integrating seamlessly with both Google Meet and Zoom, Beam can provide the flexibility organizations need while helping to elevate everyday conversations.

Proving our real-world impact

Through extensive internal testing at Google, we’ve learned how transformative Beam can be for areas like recruiting, talent development, and cross-functional collaboration. In a recent eight-week internal study, Google teams using Beam felt 50% more connected to one another, found it 33% easier to ensure their feedback was clearly understood, and saw a 21% drop in the need for follow-up meetings. All of this has reinforced our own belief in expanding our own deployment of Beam for Googlers, alongside our customers.

We are also working closely with leaned-in partners to prove out these exact use cases in the field. Earlier this year, we partnered with Bain and Company to test how HP Dimension with Google Beam could help transform their campus recruiting and candidate interviews. By using this technology, Bain was able to create authentic, face-to-face connections with candidates from anywhere—without the need for extensive travel. Watch how Bain is transforming their interview process here.

We are thrilled to see this excitement mirrored by other first customers like Netflix, Capital Group, and many more who are eager to transform how they connect their global workforces.

Creating the first-ever Beam extended network

To help make Beam accessible to organizations of all sizes, we are partnering with Industrious, a global operator of premium flexible workspaces worldwide. Together, we are creating the first-ever Beam extended network.

We conducted a pilot earlier this year, in which we heard firsthand how distributed teams are connecting for manager check-ins, interviews, and client consultations. Now, this network will increase access to Google Beam, opening the doors for more startups and businesses of all sizes to better connect and make their meetings feel much more natural.

Starting in October, you can book and experience HP Dimension with Google Beam directly at select Industrious locations across the U.S., including Atlanta, Chicago, New York City and Palo Alto. Learn more here.

The way we work is evolving, but the need for genuine human connection remains constant. Discover how organizations worldwide are transforming their meetings and explore more real-world use cases at beam.google.
